subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = 6i + 2j + 3k and b = 2i − 9j + 6k, find a·b and the angle between a and b.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 18(ii), book p.71. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Computed twice. Component by component: a·b = 6(2) + 2(−9) + 3(6) = 12 − 18 + 18 = 12; |a| = √(36 + 4 + 9) = √49 = 7; |b| = √(4 + 81 + 36) = √121 = 11; cos θ = 12/77. Checked a second way with the cross-product identity |a × b|² = |a|²|b|² − (a·b)²: a × b = i(12 + 27) − j(36 − 6) + k(−54 − 4) = 39i − 30j − 58k, so |a × b|² = 1521 + 900 + 3364 = 5785, while |a|²|b|² − (a·b)² = 49 × 121 − 144 = 5929 − 144 = 5785. The two agree, which confirms both a·b = 12 and the two magnitudes. Numerically Cos⁻¹(12/77) = Cos⁻¹(0.15584) ≈ 81.03°, so the card says θ ≈ 81°. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards the four separate acts: the dot product, the two magnitudes, the cosine formula, and stating both of the two things the question asks for. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors carries a Section B slot on the paper and also appears in Section C. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the dot product and then the angle between two given vectors — name each move in order.

steps.label: Find a·b
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply matching components and add. The j components are 2 and −9, so that middle term is negative — carry the sign into the sum, do not add 18.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply matching components and add: i with i, j with j, k with k.

accept: multiply matching components and add to get twelve
twelve minus eighteen plus eighteen is twelve
the dot product of a and b is twelve
matching components multiply chesi add cheste twelve vasthundi
a dot b comes to twelve

steps.why: The dot product in component form needs no angle, which is why it can be computed first and then used to find the angle rather than the other way round.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus on the j term and getting 48.
Multiplying the i of one vector by the j of the other.

steps.label: Find |a| and |b|
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both come out whole: 49 and 121 are perfect squares, so |a| = 7 and |b| = 11. If either root is not whole here, a component has been squared wrongly.
steps.memory_tip: Both magnitudes are whole numbers here: √49 = 7 and √121 = 11.

accept: mod a is root forty nine which is seven
mod b is root one hundred twenty one which is eleven
square the components add and take the root for each vector
mod a seven, mod b eleven vasthundi
both magnitudes come out as whole numbers

steps.why: The cosine formula divides the dot product by the product of the two lengths, so both lengths have to be in hand before the angle can be written.
common_mistakes: Adding the components rather than their squares.

steps.label: Write cos θ
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Denominator is 7 × 11 = 77, not 7 + 11. The fraction 12/77 does not reduce, since 77 = 7 × 11 and neither divides 12.
steps.memory_tip: cos θ = (a·b)/(|a||b|) — the lengths MULTIPLY underneath.
lines: Let θ be the angle between a and b.

accept: cos theta is the dot product over the product of the magnitudes
twelve over seven times eleven is twelve by seventy seven
cos theta equals twelve by seventy seven
cos theta ante a dot b by mod a into mod b, twelve by seventy seven
divide twelve by seventy seven

steps.why: The definition a·b = |a||b| cos θ rearranges to give cos θ directly. It is the only link between the component arithmetic already done and the angle asked for.
common_mistakes: Adding the magnitudes instead of multiplying them.

steps.label: State both answers
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The question asks for two things, so both must appear in the final line. 12/77 is not a standard cosine, so the exact answer stays as an inverse cosine.
steps.memory_tip: Two things were asked, so two things go in the final answer.
lines: small, so θ is a little under 90°:

recall.must_convey: That the two answers are a·b = 12 and θ = Cos⁻¹(12/77), roughly 81°.
accept: a dot b is twelve and the angle is cos inverse twelve by seventy seven
the angle is about eighty one degrees
state both the dot product and the angle
a dot b twelve, angle cos inverse twelve by seventy seven
cos inverse of twelve over seventy seven is roughly eighty one degrees

steps.why: A positive cosine near zero means the two vectors are close to perpendicular but not quite. Saying so is a quick check that the arithmetic is sensible before the answer is written down.
common_mistakes: Answering only the angle and forgetting a·b, or the reverse.
Writing θ = 12/77, which is a cosine and not an angle.
